newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Totta a prisoner of 1996 dividend.
newsitem.headline: Totta a prisoner of 1996 dividend.

text.p: The Lisbon market looks set to punish shares of Banco Totta e Acores until its final 1996 dividend is known, analysts said.

Totta shares plunged 10 percent in heavy trade on Monday after the bank said it planned to pay out a 1996 dividend of 135 escudos in response to a 13 percent drop in its net profit to 15 billion escudos ($93 million). Totta was expected to make a final 1996 dividend announcement in the coming weeks.
The market had expected the bank to pay around 190 escudos, in line with the 1995 payout.
"The fall of the Totta share price is essentially linked to the 1996 dividend," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Totta shares closed at 2,698 escudos, down 332, in volume of 971,995 shares on Lisbon bourse.
Another analyst said: "The share price will recover only if the final dividend exceeds the announced 135 escudos."
A third analyst said: "The main problem with Totta is that the 1996 results and dividend were worse than expected."
Majority shareholder Antonio Champalimaud said that he personally would be demanding that the bank increase "significantly" the level of dividend that it was proposing to pay.
Analysts said Totta was a prisoner of its "dividend yield."
They said that if Totta's final 1996 dividend were 135 escudos, its dividend yield would stand at five percent. If the dividend were 190 escudos, the dividend yield would be six percent.

One analyst said: "On Friday, before the announcement of the 135 escudos dividend, when the share price was 3,030 escudos (200 escudos less than in the previous session), the dividend yield was 6.3 percent."
He added: "The board will make its final dividend announcement as soon as possible to clear things up completely."
Analysts said Totta was known for paying out a generous dividend.
"135 escudos is a good dividend but it is not equivalent to what the company would normally pay out," said one analyst.
